noteBlocks.md:
Walk 3 km east and then 4 km north. The **distance** you covered is $3 + 4 = 7$ km, because distance follows the path.

Your **displacement** is the single straight step from start to finish: $5$ km, on a bearing of $037^{\circ}$ — between north and east. Both numbers are true, and they answer different questions.

noteBlocks.explain: She finishes at the start, so the straight line between them has no length. The distance she ran is still 400 m.

noteBlocks.md:
A **vector quantity has magnitude and direction**. A **scalar quantity has magnitude only**. Magnitude just means the size of the thing, and examiners accept the word *quantity* in its place.

Write the general sentence first and then give an example. An example offered instead of a definition earns nothing, however good the example is.

noteBlocks.title: Why direction has to be part of the measure
noteBlocks.md: Two forces of 30 N do completely different things depending on where they point: pulling the same way they add to 60 N, pulling against each other they cancel. A number alone cannot tell you which happened, so the direction has to travel with the measure rather than being mentioned afterwards.

noteBlocks.explain: Magnitude and direction is the vector. Naming mass gives an example, and an example is not a definition.

noteBlocks.md:
Everyday speech uses *weight* for what a balance shows, which is really the mass. In mechanics they are separate: mass is how much matter there is, in kilograms, and weight is the force gravity exerts on it, in newtons.

Gravity pulls downwards, so weight has a direction and is a vector. Mass points nowhere, so it is a scalar. This is the single most misclassified measure on the paper.

noteBlocks.explain: The sand is the same sand, so the mass is the same. The Moon pulls on it less hard, so the force on it is smaller.

Tension is a force, so it goes with the vectors. Energy is a single amount in joules, so it goes with the scalars.

steps.decision: Distance adds up the whole path, whichever way each piece went, because it has no direction attached to it.

options: Because distance measures the path travelled, with no direction attached
Because distance is always the shortest route between two points
Because distance and displacement are two words for the same measure
whyMenu.explain: The shortest route is the displacement. Distance follows the path she actually rode, so a journey that doubles back keeps adding.

steps.working: Displacement $= 5$ km on a bearing of $036.87^{\circ}$, since $\sqrt{3^2 + 4^2} = 5$.
steps.decision: Displacement is one straight step from the start to the finish, so it needs both a size and a direction to be stated in full.

steps.working: A vector quantity has magnitude and direction. Her displacement is one.
steps.decision: CCEA wants a general definition, not an example standing in for one. Give the definition first, then name an example.

steps.working: A scalar quantity has magnitude only. The distance she rode is one.
steps.decision: Magnitude means the size of the quantity. A scalar stops there; nothing about direction is part of it.

items.stem: A runner does one full lap of a 400 m track and stops where she started. What are her distance and her displacement?
